name: Archibald Crane
bio: Lord Blackwood's loud, cigar-chomping business partner, staying the night. Wears a waistcoat under considerable strain.

personality.speechStyle: Booming City bluster: short barked sentences, trade slang, rhetorical questions and plenty of 'old boy'. Gets louder and redder when cornered, and answers a hard question by attacking the person asking it.
tells: mops his brow with a huge handkerchief

goals: Protect his name and his seat on the board
Wriggle out of any blame for his outburst at dinner
Steer the household's suspicion towards somebody else

beliefs.statement: That gardener did it. Turns up soaked and shifty the moment the body is found.
Victoria stayed by the dining-room fire all the while I was away, from 21:13 until I came back at 21:22.
The butler was listening at his door so he could report me to the police.

secrets.description: He embezzled company money, and during the blackout he telephoned his broker to move it before midnight.
secrets.testimonySummary: Mr Crane admits he embezzled company money, and that between 21:15 and 21:20 he telephoned his broker to move it before midnight.

secrets.description: He was not with Victoria in the dining room from 21:13 to 21:22. He left two minutes after Reginald lit the candles, was on the servants' telephone from 21:15 to 21:20 and was back at 21:22. He agreed to her story at 21:40 to hide the call.
secrets.testimonySummary: Mr Crane admits he left the dining room at 21:13, after the candles were lit, and was back at 21:22. He used the servants' telephone 21:15-21:20; the butler called through the pantry door at 21:18. At 21:40 he backed Lady Victoria's story.

relationships.description: Old friend and business partner. Their quarrels were loud, frequent and, he insists, only ever about business.
Treats her as a grieving ornament: decorative, dramatic and not to be taken seriously. Underneath, he is wary of how sharp she is when she thinks nobody is looking.

jabs.text: Bearing up awfully well for a new widow, Victoria. Quite the little trouper.
Funny how you always know where everyone was, when you were so busy swooning.

defensiveOn.text: He laughs too loudly, calls it business, and tells her not to trouble her pretty head.

relationships.description: Thinks him a stiff-necked busybody who forgets his place. Bluster is his first answer to anything the butler says.

jabs.text: It was your candlestick, Reginald. You lit it, you carried it, you fussed over it in front of all of us.
A butler who remembers every word at dinner knows an awful lot for a man who only carries trays.

defensiveOn.text: He goes beetroot red and demands to know who pays the wages in this house.

relationships.description: Barely notices him until there is a body, then finds him very convenient: the man with the mud on his boots and the face of a guilty spaniel.

jabs.text: You turned up soaked and shifty the moment the body was found, man. What were you doing out in that weather?
Speak up, man! Mumbling into your cap won't wash with me.

defensiveOn.text: He talks straight over him and starts pointing again.

intendedLies.claim: I was with Victoria by the dining-room fire from the moment the candles were lit until the scream. Ask her!
The row at dinner? A racehorse, old boy. Purely sporting.
